sn22.122:1.1: At one time Venerable Sāriputta and Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita were staying near Varanasi, in the deer park at Isipatana.
sn22.122:1.2: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita came out of retreat, went to Venerable Sāriputta, and said:
sn22.122:1.3: “Reverend Sāriputta, what things should an ethical meditator rationally apply the mind to?”
sn22.122:1.4: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, an ethical meditator should rationally apply the mind to the five grasping aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, as diseased, as a boil, as a dart, as gloom, as an affliction, as alien, as breaking apart, as empty, as not-self.
sn22.122:1.6: That is, the grasping aggregates of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.
sn22.122:1.7: An ethical meditator should rationally apply the mind to these five grasping aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, as diseased, as a boil, as a dart, as gloom, as an affliction, as alien, as breaking apart, as empty, as not-self.
sn22.122:1.8: It’s possible that an ethical meditator who rationally applies the mind to the five grasping aggregates will realize the fruit of stream-entry.”
sn22.122:2.1: “But Reverend Sāriputta, what things should a meditator stream-enterer rationally apply the mind to?”
sn22.122:2.2: “A meditator stream-enterer should also rationally apply the mind to these five grasping aggregates as impermanent … as not-self.
sn22.122:2.3: It’s possible that a meditator stream-enterer who rationally applies the mind to the five grasping aggregates will realize the fruit of once-return.”
sn22.122:3.1: “But Reverend Sāriputta, what things should a meditator once-returner rationally apply the mind to?”
sn22.122:3.2: “A meditator once-returner should also rationally apply the mind to these five grasping aggregates as impermanent … as not-self.
sn22.122:3.3: It’s possible that a meditator once-returner who rationally applies the mind to the five grasping aggregates will realize the fruit of non-return.”
sn22.122:4.1: “But Reverend Sāriputta, what things should a meditator non-returner rationally apply the mind to?”
sn22.122:4.2: “A meditator non-returner should also rationally apply the mind to these five grasping aggregates as impermanent … as not-self.
sn22.122:4.3: It’s possible that a meditator non-returner who rationally applies the mind to the five grasping aggregates will realize perfection.”
sn22.122:5.1: “But Reverend Sāriputta, what things should a perfected one rationally apply the mind to?”
sn22.122:5.2: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, a perfected one should also rationally apply the mind to the five grasping aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, as diseased, as a boil, as a dart, as gloom, as an affliction, as alien, as breaking apart, as empty, as not-self.
sn22.122:5.3: A perfected one has nothing more to do, and nothing that needs improvement.
sn22.122:5.4: Still, these things, when developed and cultivated, lead to blissful meditation in this life, and also to mindfulness and comprehension.”
